title: Preference-Aware Heterogeneous Goal Adaptation for LLM Agent Workflows
research_question: Can a MAPE-K-style controller with Bayesian model averaging over candidate workflow models improve task success and reduce unnecessary re-planning in multi-agent LLM workflows when user preferences combine threshold and optimization goals?
hypothesis: Existing adaptive workflow methods under-handle heterogeneous requirements, while Bayesian model averaging has shown promise for self-adaptive systems but has not been convincingly transferred to multi-agent LLM workflows; incorporating explicit threshold and optimization goals into a preference-aware adaptation loop will improve decision quality under uncertainty.
motivation: The knowledge base highlights an open problem in self-adaptive systems: extending Bayesian model averaging approaches to heterogeneous requirements such as threshold and optimization goals. At the same time, several nearby agentic workflow ideas were already rejected for limited novelty, especially around generic uncertainty-aware scheduling, adaptive decomposition, and routing. This creates a specific research gap: instead of proposing another scheduler, investigate whether a preference-aware adaptation controller can transfer a validated self-adaptive systems mechanism into multi-agent LLM orchestration, where workflows must satisfy mixed constraints like latency/cost ceilings while optimizing quality. This is both grounded by explicit future-work evidence and differentiated from rejected ideas by focusing on heterogeneous requirement modeling rather than generic routing or scheduling.
